recipes.name: Gozleme!!
ingredients: 1/2 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt ((halve for table salt, +50% for flakes))
250g / 8 oz Danish feta (the soft feta) or Greek feta ((Note 2))
400g / 14 oz beef or lamb mince ((ground meat))
1 small red capsicum / bell pepper (, diced)
1/4 tsp cayenne ((mild spiciness, can leave out))
3/4 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt ((halve for table salt, +50% for flakes))
120g / 4 oz Danish feta (soft) or Greek feta ((Note 2))
instructions: Put all dough ingredients in stand mixer and knead 2 1/2 min on speed 7. Rest 20 min, cut into 4, roll out into 35 x 20cm/14" x 8". Top with fillings, fold to seal, pan fry golden on medium high, 3 min each side.

Make dough - Fit stand mixer with dough hook. Combine flour, oil, salt and water in the stand mixer bowl. Mix for 2 1/2 minutes on medium high speed 7 until smooth (see video for before & after). (Note 4) Dough should be a pliable, smooth ball, not sticky. (Adjust with sprinkle of water if dry, or flour if sticky).Food processor option - Use the standard metal "S" blade, put everything in then blitz 30 sec until a dough ball forms. Or knead by hand ~ 5min.
Rest 20 min - Cover the bowl with the dough in it and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll out - Sprinkle work surface with flour. Cut dough into 4 pieces. Roll each out into 35 x 20cm/14" x 8" rectangles.
Make EITHER the lamb / beef Filling, or Spinach & Feta (or make 1/2 batch of both!).
Cook - Heat oil in large skillet over high heat. Cook garlic and onion for 1 minute. Add capsicum, cook for 2 minutes. Add beef and cook until it changes from pink to brown, breaking it up as you go.
Spices and spinach - Add cumin, paprika, cayenne (if using), salt, pepper and water. Cook for 2 minutes. Add spinach, stir until wilted.
Scrunch - Place spinach, garlic, egg and pepper in a bowl. Scrunch with hands to reduce volume and make spinach "floppy". (Makes it easier to fold and seal).
Feta last - Crumble fat in and stir through, trying not to turn it into mush. Cheese gets added when assembling.
Spread Filling on half the pastry, pushing to the edge. Sprinkle Lamb/Beef Filling with crumbled feta. Sprinkle Spinach Feta with mozzarella cheese.
Seal - Fold other side of pastry over to cover Filling. Press down edges, pressing out excess air pockets trapped inside as you go. Use water if needed to seal well.
Transfer - Sprinkle flour on a round pizza paddle (or similar). Slide gozleme onto paddle. (This is for ease of transferring into pan).
Heat 1 1/2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium high heat. (I usually get 2 pans going). Don't skimp on oil else your gozleme will just burn instead of going golden and crisp.
Cook until golden - Slide gozleme into skillet. Cook, lightly pressing down (including edges), until deep golden and crispy - about 3 minutes. Flip and cook, pressing down lightly, until crispy.
Cut and serve - Transfer to cutting board. Cut into 6 or 8 pieces. Serve immediately with lemon wedges, if desired.

page_recipe_notes: Recipe Notes: 1. Filling – choose either Spinach Feta OR Spiced Lamb/Beef. Filling is enough to fill 4 gozlemes. OR make a half batch of each which is what I usually do – use recipe scaler to scale ingredients down (click on Servings and slide down until beef reaches 250g/0.5lb and everything will change). 2. Danish Feta – a soft feta that is like a cross between greek feta and goats cheese. Ideal for Gozleme but normal feta totally fine. 3. Mozzarella cheese – not usually in Gozleme so it’s optional. But I can’t resist! 4. Dough – Soft, pliable but not sticky – very easy to handle. Adjust with sprinkle of extra flour or water if needed to achieve consistency shown in video. Hand kneading – about 6 to 7 minutes. Gluten free flour – works great! Dough is not as stretchy, it’s more like short pastry (like Quiche , see video). Also recommend making 5 smaller ones rather than 4, for ease of handling. Pastry does not brown as well, but flavour and texture is the same! 5. Storage / reheating: Cooked gozleme should be eaten asap while hot and crispy! Dough can be kept for 3 days in fridge, after doing the 20 minute rest on the counter. Do not keep filled uncooked gozleme in fridge – inside sweats and makes underside of dough soggy Best way to keep warm while you keep cooking is in 120C/250F oven ON A RACK not on a baking tray (hot gozleme sweats and underside gets soggy) Cooked gozleme can be frozen or kept in fridge – cool, wrap, put in container Reheat either by pan frying (best way, for crispiness) or on tray in oven at 180C/350F for 7 minutes or so 6. Pastry and fillings adapted from this recipe from Gourmet Wog . It’s the one I’ve been using exclusively since I found it. 7. Calories per gozleme – Spinach and Feta. There’s a fair amount of olive oil in Gozleme, but remember olive oil is better for you than other oils! Don’t be tempted to cut down on the fat in the pastry. But you can cook with less – spray a non stick pan.
